Sanjay Vashisth, J. (Oral)
1.
Instant appeal has been filed by the appellant - New India Assurance Company Ltd., by challenging the award dated 28.10.2004, passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal,
Fatehabad (for brevity, 'Ld. Tribunal'), whereby, MAC Case No. 73 of 2001, filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, 'MV Act'), claiming compensation on account of damage of car to the tune of Rs.5.00 lakhs, has been partly allowed.
From the oral as well as documentary evidence i.e. Bills Ex.P3 to Ex.P12, prayer in regard to the repair of the car in question, Ld. Tribunal calculated the amount as Rs.34,308/-.
However, to make out said calculation in round figure, the claimant i.e. respondent No.1 - Smt. Dayawanti was held to be entitled for an amount of Rs.35,000/-, as compensation on account of the damage to the car.
2. Accident in question took place on 03.10.2000 and as per the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company, 1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120533 FAO-213-2005 (O&M) -2- original licence was valid for the period i.e. 20.08.1993 to 19.08.1999 and on getting the same renewed, it was re
-validated from 20.02.2001 to 01.01.2003.
However, on being asked by the court, as to when the application for renewal of the said licence was moved, counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company, expresses his inability, as there is no such evidence available on record.

Considering the facts in its totality that the accident took place about 24 years back and the compensation has been awarded by the Ld. Tribunal, by considering the repair bills (Ex.P3 to Ex.P12) that too, to the tune of Rs.35,000/- only, and also that there is nothing available as to when the application for renewal of licence was moved & because of efflux of time, I do not find any such material to cause interference in the findings recorded by Ld. Tribunal, at this stage.
